# Rounds Codex

> Rounds Codex is a visual medical education app for nursing students, medical students, and residents. It combines clinical condition guides, a 300-drug pharmacology reference, an expert-curated medical image atlas, NCLEX-RN and USMLE practice, and a peri-operative guide into one clinical learning system. Created by a practicing physician. Currently pre-launch — a launch list is open at https://roundscodex.com/.

## What it is
- A single, visual-first medical education app spanning the classroom, exams, the wards, and the point of care.
- Content is created by a practicing physician and reviewed for medical accuracy.
- It is an educational resource and does not replace clinical judgment, supervision, or institutional protocols.

## Who it is for
- **Nursing students** — clinical judgment, bedside priorities, focused disease guides, and NGN-style NCLEX-RN practice.
- **Medical students** — high-yield visual medicine and original USMLE-style practice for Step 1 and Step 2 CK.
- **Residents** — specialty-level references and image-rich reviews across 21 specialties.

## Key features
- Visual condition and disease guides covering ~180 conditions.
- A medical image atlas: roughly ten expert-curated images per condition (anatomy, pathophysiology, imaging, treatment, clinical pearls).
- Pharmacology reference for ~300 essential drugs (uses, dosing, half-life, adverse effects, boxed warnings, interactions).
- USMLE-style practice (Step 1, Step 2 CK) and NGN-style NCLEX-RN practice, with teaching rationales.
- Category-level performance analytics to guide what to study next.
- An operating-room / peri-operative guide (sterile technique, OR etiquette, workflow).

## Exam preparation
- **USMLE** — blueprint-weighted, original practice questions for Step 1 and Step 2 CK with explanations that teach clinical reasoning.
- **NCLEX-RN** — Next-Generation (NGN) style items focused on clinical judgment.

## Platform and availability
- Built for the web and iOS, mobile-first.
- Status: in active development (pre-launch). Pricing will be announced at launch; joining the launch list is free.
